[1/3] Plan: drive live enemy presentation from file-backed .kanim clips through AnimationLibrary + AnimationController while the sim hash stays untouched

impact_assessment.why: Keystone ships file-backed animation clips, sampling, crossfade and events, and the testbed proves them, but the game animates enemies with ad-hoc sine math and never loads a .kanim asset; the mechanic is test-only instead of a game feature.
impact_assessment.benefits: Every enemy type gains deterministic idle motion authored as data, and hit/death transitions can reuse the same controller, so presentation becomes tuneable without code edits.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: enemy node transforms and draw budgets; dependency: keystone animation modules (already in-tree); concurrency: none; state: new data/*.kanim files, shooter/anim.py, game.py, tests, README, cycles, ADR
impact_assessment.mitigation: Layer animation as uniform scale + rotation so existing flinch/death assertions keep their x==y and position invariants; failing-first tests; full suite; determinism 1800; aikit gates

[1/3] Plan: register a committed .obj cache crate through AssetRegistry.register_file (asset_io + obj_loader) and hot-reload it from the game loop

impact_assessment.why: The shooter testbed proves obj_loader, asset_io fingerprints and ReloadReport, but the game builds every mesh procedurally and never loads a file asset; the asset pipeline is test-only instead of a game feature.
impact_assessment.benefits: The ammo cache becomes a real file-backed crate, and a one-second refresh lets an artist edit the .obj without restarting, with the reload report exposed to diagnostics.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: cache node mesh and two existing cache assertions; dependency: keystone asset_io/obj_loader (in-tree); concurrency: none; state: shooter/data/cache_crate.obj, shooter/asset_pipeline.py, game.py, tests, README, cycles, ADR
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first asset tests, explicit fallback to the old cube, full suite, determinism 1800, aikit gates, README size and tree kept in budget
